cases.note: Four skills deep, which the default permits: the root counts as depth one.
Five is not four, and the fault names the whole chain rather than the last link — an operator needs to see which composition got out of hand.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"too_deep","detail":"This call chain is 5 skills deep; the limit is 4.","path":["pick","approach","align","servo","nudge"]}}

cases.note: The simplest cycle, and it is refused at install rather than discovered by a robot that has already taken a lease and started moving.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"cycle","detail":"pick is already in this call chain, so it would call itself.","path":["pick","pick"]}}

cases.note: Three skills round a loop. The repeated element is the last entry of the path, so the chain reads as the walk that found it.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"cycle","detail":"pick is already in this call chain, so it would call itself.","path":["pick","approach","retry","pick"]}}

cases.note: Two paths reaching one skill is a shared child, not a loop. An edition that marked nodes globally visited rather than tracking the current chain would refuse this, and it is legal.

A graph with both faults in it. Depth-first in declaration order reaches the cycle first, and pinning that is the point: an edition iterating its edges differently would refuse the same graph and blame a different skill, which is the half an operator reads.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"cycle","detail":"pick is already in this call chain, so it would call itself.","path":["pick","loop","pick"]}}

cases.note: A graph the root cannot reach is not this skill’s problem. Only what it can call is walked.
A skill that calls nothing composes trivially.
The root and nothing else, which is a site that has switched composition off.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"too_deep","detail":"This call chain is 2 skills deep; the limit is 1.","path":["pick","approach"]}}

cases.note: Zero would refuse the root itself, which is not a composition rule. The default is used.
An edge whose ends are not names is not an edge. Both editions discard it in `readCalls`, at the same boundary, so this case is testing one function rather than two.
cases.expected: {"fault":{"code":"cycle","detail":"pick is already in this call chain, so it would call itself.","path":["pick","pick"]}}
